title: Putnami Database Test Binding
description: A database binding extended with test provisioning and isolation policy. Uses the same datasource/connection shape as the runtime binding, so a multi-datasource workload can request migrated Postgres bindings for one or more named datasources at once — without a single-DSN env-var convention.

applyMigrations.description: When true, the provider applies and verifies migrations before returning bindings.

keepDatabases.description: When true, the provider leaves the isolated databases it created in place: the per-suite teardown closes its connections but skips DROP DATABASE. Set it when the server's own lifetime is the cleanup (e.g. a CI server that dies with the run) — every DROP forces an immediate cluster-wide checkpoint that stalls behind concurrent writes.

databases.description: Resolved datasources, keyed by logical datasource name.

datasourceName.description: Canonical logical datasource identifier: lowercase letters, digits, '-', '_', '.', '/'; 1–64 chars.

engine.description: Database engine. Closed enum; postgres is the only v1 implementation and adding an engine requires a protocol version bump.

schemaName.description: Owning schema / search_path entry; an unquoted SQL identifier. Required for postgres.

mode.description: Provider behavior when no usable binding/provider exists. Closed enum.

isolation.description: Per-datasource isolation boundary the provider creates. Closed enum.

database.description: One datasource's resolved binding: engine, schema, and the physical connection.

connection.description: Resolved physical connection. Declares exactly one transport strategy: a self-contained 'dsn'; or a structured TCP connection keyed by 'host'; or a cloud/provider socket keyed by 'instance'. A 'dsn' is self-contained and accepts no structured field. The exactly-one-transport and dsn-self-containment rules are enforced by the strict validator.

dsn.description: Self-contained connection string. Mutually exclusive with every other field.

database.description: Physical database name (structured or instance strategy).

ssl.description: Request TLS for the structured (TCP) strategy.

instance.description: Cloud/provider instance identifier for the socket strategy.
